```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```


```{r}
data <- read_csv("~/Data Science Toolbox/sprint1/hotel_bookings_clean.csv")

train <- subset(data, split == "train")
validation <- subset(data, split == "validation")
test <- subset(data, split == "test")
```

```{r}
# Check the column names
names(data)

# Check how the data has been divided
table(data$split)

# Check cancellation rates in training and validation
data %>%
  filter(split != "test") %>%
  group_by(split) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    cancellation_rate = mean(is_canceled)
  )
```

```{r}
ggplot(train, aes(
  x = hotel,
  fill = factor(is_canceled)
)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 1: Bookings by hotel and outcome",
    x = "Hotel",
    y = "Number of bookings",
    fill = "Cancelled"
  ) +
  scale_fill_discrete(
    labels = c("No", "Yes")
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
train %>%
  group_by(hotel) %>%
  summarise(
    bookings = n(),
    cancellation_rate = mean(is_canceled)
  )
```

```{r}
train <- train %>%
  mutate(
    lead_band = cut(
      lead_time,
      breaks = c(-1, 7, 30, 90, 180, 365, Inf),
      labels = c(
        "0-7", "8-30", "31-90",
        "91-180", "181-365", "365+"
      )
    )
  )
```

```{r}
lead_summary <- train %>%
  group_by(lead_band, hotel) %>%
  summarise(
    cancellation_rate = mean(is_canceled),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
ggplot(
  lead_summary,
  aes(
    x = lead_band,
    y = cancellation_rate,
    colour = hotel,
    group = hotel
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 2: Cancellation rate by lead time",
    x = "Lead time (days)",
    y = "Cancellation rate",
    colour = "Hotel"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
plot_cancellation <- function(variable) {

  summary_data <- train %>%
    group_by(category = .data[[variable]]) %>%
    summarise(
      cancellation_rate = mean(is_canceled),
      n = n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    filter(n >= 100)

  ggplot(
    summary_data,
    aes(
      x = reorder(category, cancellation_rate),
      y = cancellation_rate
    )
  ) +
    geom_col() +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(
      title = paste("Cancellation rate by", variable),
      x = NULL,
      y = "Cancellation rate"
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    theme_minimal()
}
```

```{r}
plot_cancellation("deposit_type")
```

```{r}
plot_cancellation("market_segment")
```

```{r}
plot_cancellation("customer_type")
```

```{r}
top_countries <- train %>%
  count(country, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  pull(country)
```

```{r}
train %>%
  filter(country %in% top_countries) %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(
    cancellation_rate = mean(is_canceled),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = reorder(country, cancellation_rate),
    y = cancellation_rate
  )) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 4: Cancellation rates by country",
    x = "Country",
    y = "Cancellation rate"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
seasonal_data <- train %>%
  mutate(
    month = factor(
      arrival_date_month,
      levels = month.name
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(arrival_date_year, month) %>%
  summarise(
    cancellation_rate = mean(is_canceled),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
ggplot(
  seasonal_data,
  aes(
    x = month,
    y = cancellation_rate,
    colour = factor(arrival_date_year),
    group = arrival_date_year
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 5: Cancellation rates by month and year",
    x = "Arrival month",
    y = "Cancellation rate",
    colour = "Year"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
numeric_data <- train %>%
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  select(-arrival_date_year)

cor_matrix <- cor(numeric_data)
```

```{r}
cor_data <- as.data.frame(as.table(cor_matrix))

names(cor_data) <- c(
  "Variable1",
  "Variable2",
  "Correlation"
)
ggplot(cor_data, aes(
  x = Variable1,
  y = Variable2,
  fill = Correlation
)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "blue",
    mid = "white",
    high = "red",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-1, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 6: Correlation matrix",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 90,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )
```
